prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Scottish National Party Manifesto 1997 — Summary (under 500 words)

Core message
- Yes We Can: Scotland is wealthy, pays its way, and should be independent to use its resources for jobs, public services and social justice. Only the SNP offers a clear, costed route.

Independence and constitution
- Route: SNP majority MPs trigger talks with the UK and EU, followed by a single-question referendum within 6–12 months; upon approval, independence is declared and fresh elections held.
- EU: Scotland to be a full EU member with voting rights and veto; open border with England.
- Governance: Written constitution and Bill of Rights; unicameral parliament elected by proportional representation; votes from age 16; petition-led legislation; no House of Lords; local government protected and elected by PR.
- Monarchy reformed; Chancellor of the Parliament as acting head of state in Scotland.

Economy, jobs, and tax
- Aim: Full employment, competitiveness, and social partnership (Social Chapter, trade union rights, minimum wage at half median male earnings).
- Business tax cuts phased over four years: corporation tax to 30%; small companies to 18%; abolish Class IV NICs; banded business rates; limit business rate rises to RPI.
- Investment: Exports unit; research and development; tourism boost; skills foundation; defence diversification; transport and communications upgrades.
- Personal tax: 15p starter rate; widen basic-rate band by 15%; remove NI ceiling for high earners; cut VAT on domestic fuel to 5%.

Social justice, health, and safety
- Child Benefit to £12.50; restore benefits for 16–17s.
- Pensioners’ package: pension increases, Cold Climate Allowance, remove utility standing charges, end means-testing for residential care.
- NHS: End internal market; integrate services; +£35m/year; dentistry back into NHS; ban tobacco ads and raise duties; national food and consumer health agency.
- Crime: Support “zero tolerance” of community crime; alternatives to prison; drug demand reduction and rehabilitation; handgun ban; improve courts and Procurator Fiscal service.

Education, housing, culture
- Schools: +700 teachers; repair schools; internet and computers in classrooms.
- Early years: Free nursery for all 3–4-year-olds; end vouchers.
- Students and skills: Restore maintenance grants (1990 real terms); expanded training and apprenticeships.
- Language and inclusion: Support Gaelic/Scots; ring-fenced Gaelic-medium funds; accommodate Islamic studies.
- Housing: Transfer 75% of council housing debt to central government; build 20,000 affordable homes in four years; upgrade substandard stock; protect new/renovated social housing from discounted right to buy; new accountable housing agency.
- Culture and media: Public Scottish Broadcasting Corporation (licence-fee funded); film incentives and “Scottish Screen”; “Scot-Lot” lottery with fairer distribution.

Land, rural economy, environment, energy, transport
- Land reform: Abolish feudal tenure; land register; local control of foreshore/seabed; improved access.
- Agriculture and fisheries: BSE traceability; CAP reform; rural diversification fund; fisheries regional management; processing support; stronger enforcement and research.
- Forestry: Double woodland in 25 years; native species focus.
- Environment: Stronger SEPA; national environmental targets; end nuclear reprocessing at Dounreay; renewables R&D hub.
- Energy: Secure Scotland’s share of North Sea assets (equidistance); stable oil/gas regime; tackle discriminatory gas pricing; phase out nuclear power; develop renewables and conservation.
- Transport: Public ownership of Scottish Railtrack assets; electrify key lines; integrate buses; abolish Skye Bridge tolls (shadow tolls then public ownership); support ferries; adjust Air Passenger Duty for remote areas.

Europe, world, defence, aid
- Diplomatic presence focused on trade and citizens; join Commonwealth, Council of Europe, UN; propose Association of States of the British Isles.
- Defence: Professional Scottish Defence Forces (army, navy, air force) using existing bases; peacekeeping college; remove Trident; phased NATO withdrawal while cooperating via EU/WEU/OSCE/PfP; defence diversification and Rosyth refit priority.
- Overseas aid: Grow to 0.7% of GDP within six years.

Paying for it
- Fully costed four-year budget: lever Scotland’s fiscal surplus, growth effects, defence savings, and debt-interest savings; invest in services and jobs; repay £6.6bn of UK debt share over four years.
